meaning: Rounded figure for the 186,400 registered men in Judah's camp
description: The number 186,000 is an approximation of the 186,400 registered given in Numbers 2:9 for Judah's camp. This camp consisted of three tribes: Judah (74,600), Issachar (54,400) and Zebulun (57,400), and was clearly the largest of the four camp groups that surrounded the tabernacle in the wilderness. Judah's camp was positioned on the east side of the tabernacle, facing the sunrise, and had the honorable task of breaking camp first when the people were on the march. The size and prominent position of the camp reflect Judah tribe's leading role among Israel's twelve tribes — a role that also pointed forward to the royal and messianic line that would come through Judah.

versions.meaning: The number of registered men in Judah's camp
versions.description: The number 186,000 appears in Numbers 2:9, where it states that the total number mustered in Judah's camp was 186,400. This camp consisted of three tribes: Judah (74,600), Issachar (54,400) and Zebulun (57,400), and was clearly the largest of the four camp groups surrounding the tabernacle in the wilderness. Judah's camp was positioned on the east side of the tabernacle, facing the sunrise, and had the honorable task of breaking camp first when the people were on the march. The size and prominent position of the camp reflect the leading role of the tribe of Judah among Israel's twelve tribes — a role that also pointed forward to the royal and messianic line that would come through Judah.

footnotes.text: The exact number in Numbers 2:9 is 186,400. Rounding to 186,000 may appear in various references, but the original text specifies "one hundred and eighty-six thousand and four hundred".

In rabbinic tradition, Judah's camp position toward the east holds great significance, as east is the direction of sunrise and symbolizes God's glory and light. That Judah led the advance was seen as a foreshadowing of the royal role later given to the tribe of Judah (Gen 49:10).

The four camp groups around the tabernacle (Judah, Reuben, Ephraim, and Dan) are linked in Jewish tradition to the four living creatures in Ezekiel's vision (Ezek 1:10), where Judah's camp is often associated with the lion.
